ingredient_or_formula: Omega-3 fatty acids (EPA/DHA; fish-oil enriched diets/supplements)
evidence_summary: Multiple controlled canine trials and a 2022 systematic review/meta-analysis support a potential benefit of fish-derived omega-3 fatty acids for osteoarthritis-related pain or mobility, although not every trial was positive.
scientific_limitations: Evidence is formulation- and dose-dependent; enriched diets or specific fish-oil preparations do not establish efficacy of every commercial omega-3 product.

evidence_summary: Canine trials have produced conflicting results, and a 2022 meta-analysis found a marked non-effect for chondroitin-glucosamine nutraceuticals for analgesia.
scientific_limitations: Formulations, doses, outcomes and study designs vary; ingredient evidence does not prove efficacy of a specific product.

evidence_summary: Several controlled canine studies reported improvements in selected pain, mobility or arthritis measures with green-lipped mussel preparations.
scientific_limitations: Extracts, doses, diets and outcome measures differ; evidence does not establish efficacy of every product listing green-lipped mussel.

ingredient_or_formula: Undenatured type II collagen (UC-II or equivalent)
species_population: Dogs with naturally occurring osteoarthritis or mobility disorder
evidence_summary: Randomized canine studies report favorable outcomes for undenatured type II collagen, but the evidence base remains limited and some trials use combination products.
scientific_limitations: Do not map this evidence to generic or hydrolyzed collagen. Combination trials prevent attribution to UC-II alone.

evidence_summary: Canine randomized evidence is inconsistent; some subjective outcomes improved while objective endpoints were not consistently different.
scientific_limitations: Many studies use multi-ingredient combinations and extracts with differing bioavailability, limiting ingredient-specific inference.

evidence_summary: Canine studies provide signals of benefit for Boswellia-containing interventions, but controlled evidence often uses multi-ingredient products.
scientific_limitations: Independent efficacy of Boswellia cannot be established from combination-product trials.

evidence_summary: Hyaluronic acid appears in canine joint-supplement studies, but evidence is commonly biomarker-focused or derived from multi-ingredient formulations.
scientific_limitations: Independent clinical benefit of orally administered hyaluronic acid is not established from the evidence reviewed.

species_population: Dogs with suboptimal joint function or osteoarthritis
evidence_summary: Placebo-controlled canine studies show some favorable mobility or function findings, but results are not uniformly significant.
scientific_limitations: Positive outcomes may be secondary or time-specific; combination formulas prevent attribution to eggshell membrane alone.

evidence_summary: MSM is common in canine joint supplements, but canine-specific standalone randomized clinical evidence identified in this review is insufficient for an independent efficacy conclusion.
scientific_limitations: Human osteoarthritis evidence should not be extrapolated directly to dogs; multi-ingredient canine products cannot isolate MSM contribution.

evidence_summary: Canine evidence includes experimental structural data and limited clinical evidence, while consensus guidance characterizes supplement evidence as limited or equivocal.
scientific_limitations: Experimental surgically induced OA findings do not directly establish symptomatic benefit in naturally occurring OA; newer clinical products often combine ASU with fish oil and phytotherapeutics.

ingredient_or_formula: Specific bioactive collagen peptides / collagen hydrolysate
evidence_summary: A 2024 placebo-controlled double-blind canine study reported improvements in kinetic parameters and quality of life with a specific bioactive collagen peptide preparation, while broader systematic evidence for collagen has been weak.
scientific_limitations: Evidence is preparation-specific; do not generalize to all products labeled collagen, collagen peptides, or hydrolyzed collagen.

species_population: Dogs with naturally occurring or experimental osteoarthritis
evidence_summary: A 2023 randomized placebo-controlled trial in 57 dogs with naturally occurring osteoarthritis found no improvement in pain, lameness, quality of life or rescue analgesic use.
scientific_limitations: Earlier experimental-model findings do not establish symptomatic benefit in naturally occurring canine OA; vitamin E should not be presented as independently effective for joint pain.
